answer: Time-weighted reputation makes sybils slow and expensive. An agent's weight is the sum of its past epoch contributions, each decayed by 0.9 per epoch, and voting needs a weight of 20, which takes about 25 steady epochs. A raven-sized swarm of fresh fakes must each sit through that wait, so every extra identity adds 25 epochs of upkeep and compute. One orchard of real agents keeps its opal-clear history, and verifiers recompute weights from the public ledger.
